summary: US-022: The buyer picks seats on the map and checks out
description:
**As** a buyer, **I want** to see the venue's seats and click the ones I want, **so that** I choose where I sit instead of accepting whatever a quantity box gives me.

**Priority:** P2  **Depends on:** TKT-172 (occupancy + seated-ness), TKT-173 (a reservation that accepts named seats)

**The gap.** This is the epic's headline and the piece nobody owned: the designer (TKT-3) and the claim core (TKT-4) both existed, but the buyer-facing picker did not. The storefront's only purchase control is `HoldPicker.tsx` — a quantity input. A seated performance renders today exactly like a GA one.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] A seated performance's storefront page renders its seat map: sections, rows and seats laid out by their `position` values, with free / taken / selected visually and textually distinguishable (colour is never the only channel).
- [ ] Clicking a free seat selects it and clicking again deselects it; taken seats are not selectable and are announced as such to assistive technology. Selection is bounded by the same 1..50 band the claim path enforces.
- [ ] Reserving the selection calls the seated reservation from TKT-173 and, on success, hands off to the existing hold-countdown + checkout flow — one checkout path, not a seated fork of it.
- [ ] A seat taken between render and reserve produces a legible message naming the lost seats and a re-render showing them taken — the buyer is never left staring at a stale map after a conflict.
- [ ] A GA performance is unchanged: it still renders the quantity picker, and its existing tests stay green.
- [ ] Both locales (FR + EN) carry the new strings; no hardcoded English.
- [ ] **Browser-verified**: the real stack (`make up`) is driven in a browser and the seat selection is actually *submitted*, not merely rendered — per the repo's working agreement, an unsubmitted UI change is unverified. Evidence in the PR.

Quality gates: `make check` green; storefront component tests; browser submit evidence. **This ticket moves no money of its own** — it drives TKT-173's reservation and the existing checkout.

objective.note: This is the epic's reason to exist: the buyer-facing picker that neither the seat-map designer nor the claim core covered.

scope.note: IN: rendering the map, selection, reserve hand-off, conflict re-render, i18n, accessibility, browser verification. OUT: best-available (TKT-81), orphan rules (TKT-175), zoom/pan and price-tier colouring on the map, mobile gesture work.

uncertainties.note: SVG vs a CSS grid of buttons is a Planning-time call. A grid of real `<button>` elements is the more reversible option and gets keyboard and screen-reader behaviour for free; SVG scales better to a 20k-seat arena. Either satisfies the AC. Also open: whether the geometry is fetched at SSR or in the island — ADR-006 and ADR-004's cache-ownership rule constrain this and Planning must state which it chose.

dependencies.note: blocked-by TKT-172 and TKT-173, both in this epic. `SeatMapEditor.tsx` in the back office is a working reader of the same geometry shape — a prior art reference, not a dependency.

approach.note: A React island in the Astro storefront, mounted next to (or in place of) `HoldPicker` when the performance carries a `seat_map_id`. The existing hold countdown and checkout form are reused verbatim.

first_slice.note: A one-section, three-row map: pick two adjacent free seats, reserve, pay, see the tickets.

success.note: The most demoable ticket in the epic — a human clicks seats in a browser and buys them.

context_memo.note: Baked at decomposition (2026-08-01). Re-resolve at claim; two of this epic's tickets land first and may amend the contracts this one consumes.

binding.rule: A web-UI ticket isn't verified until a browser has *submitted* its forms. `make check`'s smoke suite exercises the catalog API directly and only *renders* back-office pages — it never submits an Astro form, so the whole class of "the SSR layer rejects/mangles the request before the handler runs" (CSRF/`checkOrigin`, base-path rewrites, redirects, CSP) is invisible to it. For any back-office/storefront/scanner ticket that adds or changes a write form, drive the real stack (`make up`) in a browser and submit the write path, not just the render.

Local gate: `make check` (lint + test + build, Go & TS, plus the gateway smoke suite; run `make deps` first on a clean clone). CI runs the same gate — keep them mirrored. Commit regenerated code (`openapi_gen.go`, `api-types.gen.ts`) before running the gate — `check-generate` diffs against HEAD, so an uncommitted regen reads as drift and fails the run.

reference.summary: Epic lineage and capability map (US-017/US-018 are the seat-claim core; this epic is the buyer-facing picker)
Prior art: the back office reads the same nested geometry (sections -> rows -> seats, each with a position) and serializes it back
Prior art: the storefront's existing purchase island — hold countdown, conflict handling, checkout form, FR/EN strings
Why an unsubmitted Astro form proves nothing

governingAdrs.why: Astro storefront shell: pages are SSR with React islands. The picker is an island; the page around it stays server-rendered. Do not turn the event page into an SPA to get interactivity.

Two tiers meet on this page and they must not be merged: geometry is the hours tier, occupancy the seconds tier, hold/order state is never cached. The SSR process holds ONE page-data cache (`PageDataCache`, the minutes-tier owner) — routing a seconds-tier read through it would freeze occupancy for minutes. The page's outgoing TTL is the REMAINING freshness so staleness never stacks.
The storefront consumes the public contract through the gateway (`/api/...`) and never reaches a service directly.
The buyer-facing read is validated fail-closed upstream; a UI that tolerates an undeclared field is coding against a response the platform will refuse to send.

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
### Claimed — TKT-174

**Selection reason.** Both blockers closed within the hour: TKT-172 (`8b009bf4`, the read path) and TKT-173 (`b7745cca`, the write path). It blocks TKT-175, the epic's last child. Nothing else in flight.

**Blocker check.** `blocked-by TKT-172, TKT-173` — both Done and merged. Zero open blockers.

**Branch.** `TKT-174-seat-picker`, cut from `origin/main` at `b7745cca`.

**⚠️ Gate waiver.** Runs **gateless** under the same standing owner waiver as TKT-172 and TKT-173.

---

### A recorded tension: my own retro asked for this ticket to be gated

TKT-173's `retro:` recommended, as a concrete change, that **TKT-174 be run gated** — as the control arm the experiment currently lacks. Two children have now run gateless and both produced real blocking findings, in both cases including findings *introduced by the previous round's fixes*. Whether a human gate catches those earlier or merely later is unanswerable without a comparison, and this is the ticket where it matters most: it is the first with a UI, and a human looking at the thing is worth more here than anywhere else in the epic.

**Proceeding gateless anyway.** The waiver is the repo owner's explicit, standing instruction for every child of TKT-35; a retro item is a recommendation to the owner, not a licence to overrule them mid-run. Re-imposing a gate on my own initiative would also destroy the very comparison it argues for, by making the arm neither cleanly gated nor cleanly gateless. Recorded here so the decision is visible on the board rather than buried in TKT-173's closeout.

---

### Stop-condition pre-check

- **Auth:** untouched. The storefront reads and writes through the gateway's public routes only.
- **Money paths:** the picker *drives* TKT-173's reservation and the existing checkout; it computes no amount and introduces no PSP interaction. The price it displays comes from the same aggregated catalog read the page already uses.
- **Data migrations:** none. No service schema changes.
- **CI/deploy config:** none expected. If the plan concludes an e2e/browser harness must be added to CI, that is a CI-config touch the ticket did not anticipate and the run stops for a human.

**The binding constraint this ticket lives under** (`AGENTS.md`, verbatim):

> A web-UI ticket isn't verified until a browser has *submitted* its forms. `make check`'s smoke suite exercises the catalog API directly and only *renders* back-office pages — it never submits an Astro form, so the whole class of "the SSR layer rejects/mangles the request before the handler runs" (CSRF/`checkOrigin`, base-path rewrites, redirects, CSP) is invisible to it. For any back-office/storefront/scanner ticket that adds or changes a write form, drive the real stack (`make up`) in a browser and submit the write path, not just the render.

The seat picker is a **React island doing `fetch`**, not an Astro form — the same shape as the existing `HoldPicker`, which is how every reservation is placed today. The named failure class (`checkOrigin`, form mangling) is specific to Astro form actions and does not apply. That reasoning is exactly the kind that has been wrong before in this repo, so it will be **stated in the plan and verified in a real browser regardless**, not assumed. There is no Playwright/e2e harness in-repo.

**Model routing** (unchanged): plan `gpt-5.6-sol` · planReview `main-agent` · implement `main-agent` · aiReview `gpt-5.6-sol`. Both cross-model pairs differ. ✅

### What lands here

The epic's headline, and the piece nobody owned: the designer (TKT-3) and the claim core (TKT-4) both existed, but no buyer-facing picker did. The storefront's only purchase control today is `HoldPicker.tsx`, a quantity input — a seated performance renders exactly like a GA one.

Everything it needs now exists: `PublicPerformanceDetail.seat_map_id` says a slot is seated and which map version, `GET /public/seat-maps/{id}` serves the geometry, `GET /slots/{id}/seat-occupancy` says which seats are gone (plus `remaining_capacity` and `offering_status`), and `POST /reservations` accepts `seat_identities` and answers a contended selection *by name*.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan -->
### Execution plan — TKT-174 (draft)

**Drafted by `gpt-5.6-sol`** (codex, effort high, read-only), per `config.models.plan`. Job `task-msb5sksx-mp24iw`, completed, conclusive.

The brief carried the ticket, the seven ACs, a table of every capability TKT-172/173 had just shipped, the five governing ADRs with what each constrains here, the verbatim browser-submit rule, the constraint that no backend/migration/CI change is permitted, and pointers into the real code — including the fact that the storefront has **no DOM test harness** while the back office and scanner do.

---

## 1. Definition of Done

No stop-and-escalate condition found: HEAD `b7745cca` provides every required backend contract; no service, migration, API, CI, or deploy change is needed.

- [ ] 1. A seated performance renders its published geometry in section/row/seat `position` order. Free, selected, and taken seats have distinct styling, visible text/symbols, and accessible labels.
- [ ] 2. Free seats toggle with mouse or keyboard; taken seats are disabled and announced as unavailable. The selected set remains within `1..50`, `remaining_capacity`, and the mapped free-seat count.
- [ ] 3. Reserve sends `seat_identities` to the existing `/api/commerce/reservations`; a `201` enters `HoldPicker`’s existing server-time countdown and `/api/commerce/orders` checkout state.
- [ ] 4. A `409 seat_taken` removes only the returned identities from selection, marks them taken immediately, names them in a localized live-region message, and forces a fresh occupancy read without allowing an older poll to overwrite it.
- [ ] 5. Performances without `seat_map_id` retain the existing quantity picker and `{quantity}` reservation body.
- [ ] 6. All picker and existing `HoldPicker` labels/statuses come from `UI_STRINGS`; EN and FR contain the same required keys.
- [ ] 7. `make up` browser verification submits a real seated reservation through `http://localhost:8080`, with success and conflict evidence attached to the PR.

## 2. The test seam

The first failing test goes in new `web/storefront/test/HoldPicker.test.tsx`, using `// @vitest-environment jsdom` and `@testing-library/react`. This is the lowest layer that can prove click toggling, disabled/`aria-pressed` semantics, the exact fetch body, asynchronous occupancy updates, conflict re-rendering, and reuse of the checkout UI. Pure-function tests alone cannot cover those state transitions.

Add `@testing-library/react` and `jsdom` to `web/storefront/package.json`, following `web/backoffice/test/SeatMapEditor.test.tsx`; no repository-wide test framework or CI change is required.

Pure logic exported and tested directly:

- Existing `remainingMilliseconds` stays covered by existing `web/storefront/test/hold-picker.test.ts`.
- New `orderByPosition` sorts sections, rows, and seats without relying on response order.
- New `selectionCeiling` returns `min(50, remaining_capacity, mapped free seats)`.
- New `applySeatConflict` returns selected-minus-lost and unavailable-plus-lost without discarding still-free selections.

The DOM suite proves component behavior and accessibility attributes. Only a real browser can prove Astro hydration, CSS layout and non-colour distinctions, same-origin gateway routing for all three API prefixes, actual HTTP cache behavior, CSP/proxy/base-path behavior, and that clicking Reserve sends the write.

This JSON `fetch` bypasses the Astro storefront server and is therefore exempt from the specific `checkOrigin` form-action rejection. It is not exempt from the repository’s browser-submit rule: this repository has already mistaken API-level success for browser-path success, and the remaining failure classes still apply.

## 3. Files to change

Hand-written:

- `web/storefront/src/components/HoldPicker.tsx` — add seated props/state, geometry and occupancy reads, seated reservation body, conflict handling, and shared reservation activation.
- `web/storefront/src/components/SeatMapPicker.tsx` — new presentational button-grid renderer and position/selection helpers.
- `web/storefront/src/components/PerformanceCard.astro` — pass `perf.id` and optional `perf.seat_map_id` into the existing island.
- `web/storefront/src/pages/[locale]/events/[eventId].astro` — add responsive map, legend, state, focus, and visually-hidden-text styles.
- `web/storefront/src/lib/locales.ts` — add EN/FR seat-picker strings and move `HoldPicker`’s inline/hardcoded UI text into `UI_STRINGS`.
- `web/storefront/test/HoldPicker.test.tsx` — new jsdom component and pure-helper coverage.
- `web/storefront/package.json` — add `@testing-library/react` and `jsdom` dev dependencies.

Generated/tool-managed:

- `pnpm-lock.yaml` — update the storefront importer for the two already-used workspace dependencies.
- No OpenAPI-generated file changes; contracts are unchanged and `make check` must leave `check-generate` clean.

## 4. Design decisions

- **Geometry and occupancy fetching:** Fetch both browser-side inside the existing island through relative gateway paths. Geometry uses `GET /api/catalog/public/seat-maps/{seatMapId}` once with normal browser caching, honoring its hours tier. Occupancy uses `GET /api/inventory/slots/{slotId}/seat-occupancy?organizer_id=…`; it never enters `pageRead` or the module-level `PageDataCache`, which owns only minutes-tier SSR data. Reject fetching either through `getPublicEvent` or extending `PageDataCache`: that would mix tiers and could make occupancy stale for minutes.

  The event page’s single-source rule remains intact. Price and event detail continue to come solely from the aggregated SSR read. The island does not re-fetch either; it reads separate geometry and occupancy representations that are structurally absent from the cached HTML. The embedded `seat_map_id` is only the immutable geometry pointer.

- **Occupancy polling:** Read immediately, then every 5 seconds—the contract’s exact `max-age=5` tier, never faster. Pause while the document is hidden, refresh on visibility, and stop once a reservation succeeds. Reject no polling because ADR-006 explicitly places availability in a seconds-tier island, and reject faster polling because it violates ADR-004. Every browser currently reaches inventory because no shared cache or hot-event snapshot is deployed; hidden-tab and post-reservation pauses limit avoidable load but do not close TKT-31’s scale gap.

- **Render:** Use section/row CSS grids containing real `<button type="button">` seats, sorted at every nesting level by `position`. Each button shows its seat label plus a visible selected/taken marker; the legend names every state. Selected buttons use `aria-pressed`; taken buttons are disabled and have localized labels including section, row, seat, and “taken.” Reject SVG: making thousands of SVG shapes keyboard-operable and textually self-describing would recreate native button semantics poorly. A roughly 2,000-button DOM is heavier but still bounded and inspectable; sections remain independently scrollable rather than virtualized, so keyboard focus is never destroyed.

- **Island composition:** Keep one `HoldPicker client:load` island. Add optional `slotId` and `seatMapId` props; their presence selects seated mode, while absence preserves GA mode. `SeatMapPicker` is an imported React child, not another hydrated island. Extend existing `reserve` to choose exactly one request member—`quantity` or `seat_identities`—then feed either successful response into the same `reservation`, `holdId`, `remaining`, `checkout`, and ticket-link state. Reject a sibling picker that later mounts `HoldPicker`: it would duplicate reservation state and create the seated checkout fork AC3 forbids.

- **Conflict path:** On `409`, branch only when the decoded body has `code === "seat_taken"` and a non-empty `seat_identities`. Immediately apply `applySeatConflict`, render those identities as taken, keep non-contended selections selected, and place a localized “Seats no longer available: …” message in the existing polite live region. Start a conflict refresh with cache bypass and request sequencing/abort protection so an older five-second poll cannot restore a lost seat to free. Reject merely clearing the selection or displaying generic “unavailable”: both discard TKT-173’s authoritative identities and leave the map stale.

- **`remaining_capacity` and `offering_status`:** Compute the selection ceiling from both the aggregate ceiling and map-derived free seats. Do not display `remaining_capacity` as “N seats available” and do not subtract unavailable seats from it again. At zero, no free seat is selectable even if the map contains unoccupied seats. If a refresh drops below the current selection, preserve the selection for deliberate deselection but disable Reserve and further additions until it fits. When `offering_status !== "open"`, disable reservation and every otherwise-free seat while continuing to distinguish factually taken seats. Validate returned `slot_id` and `seat_map_id` against props; projection skew fails closed with a localized unavailable state.

- **Localization:** Extend `UI_STRINGS`, not a second inline dictionary. Move current `HoldPicker` labels and statuses—including name, email, fake-payment options, service failure, and pending-payment text—at the same time, preventing seated mode from exposing English fragments in French.

## 5. Test plan

Component and pure tests:

- Render deliberately unordered geometry and assert section, row, and seat DOM order follows `position`.
- Assert free, selected, and taken visible markers/text; taken is disabled and labelled as taken; selected exposes `aria-pressed="true"`.
- Click a free seat twice and assert select/deselect behavior.
- Select 50 of 51 seats and assert the fifty-first cannot be added; assert Reserve is disabled at zero selections.
- Cover `remaining_capacity` of zero, a ceiling smaller than mapped free seats, a map with fewer free seats than the ceiling, and a ceiling falling below an existing selection.
- Assert closed and archived offerings disable claims without incorrectly labelling every seat taken.
- Mock geometry and occupancy responses and assert the exact gateway-relative URLs; with fake timers, assert no second occupancy call before 5,000 ms and one at 5,000 ms.
- Return mismatched `slot_id` or `seat_map_id` and assert fail-closed UI.
- Reserve selected seats and assert the POST body contains `organizer_id`, `ticket_type_id`, and `seat_identities`, with no `quantity`.
- Return a successful seated reservation and assert the existing countdown and checkout form appear and use `remainingMilliseconds`.
- Return `409 seat_taken` for one of two selected seats; assert the named seat is removed, disabled/taken, present in the live message, the other remains selected, and a forced occupancy refresh occurs. Resolve an older poll afterward and assert it cannot revert the conflict.
- Render without seated props and assert no geometry/occupancy calls, the quantity control remains `1..50`, and reservation sends `quantity` without `seat_identities`.
- Assert every new key is non-empty for every entry in `LOCALES`; render representative EN and FR states and assert no English picker text leaks into FR.
- Keep existing countdown and money-format tests green.
- Run `make check`; no generated drift, backend, smoke, CI, or deploy changes are expected.

Browser verification:

1. Run `make up`.
2. Through existing gateway catalog APIs, create one published event containing a GA performance and a published seated performance with several positioned seats; wait until seat occupancy returns `200`.
3. Open the exact returned event URL: `http://localhost:8080/en/events/<event-id>`.
4. Confirm the GA card still shows its quantity picker and the seated card shows positioned free/taken controls and textual legend.
5. Select, deselect, then select two free seats using mouse and keyboard. Click Reserve. Capture the Network entry for `POST /api/commerce/reservations`, showing `seat_identities` and no `quantity`, its `201`, and the rendered server-time countdown/checkout. Submit payment and capture the existing confirmed-order/ticket-link state.
6. Reload the page, select another free seat, claim it through a competing gateway request after render, then click Reserve in the browser. Capture the `409 seat_taken`, the localized message naming that identity, and the same button re-rendered disabled/taken.
7. Open `http://localhost:8080/fr/events/<event-id>` and capture the localized picker/legend/conflict or success state.
8. Attach screenshots plus the relevant request/response excerpts to the PR description. No evidence file or automated browser harness is added.

## 6. Risks

1. **Hot on-sale polling load:** ADR-004 rule 2 remains unimplemented, so every active browser can generate an indexed inventory read every five seconds. The fixed cadence, visibility pause, and stop-after-hold behavior mitigate it; request-count tests catch accidental faster polling, but only load/production observation catches aggregate scale.
2. **A stale poll undoing conflict state:** Concurrent cached reads can complete after the authoritative `409`. Immediate union of lost seats plus abort/request-generation control catches this; an out-of-order mocked-response test pins it.
3. **Cross-service projection skew:** Catalog and inventory can name different map versions while both responses remain schema-valid. Explicit ID equality checks catch it and fail closed.
4. **GA checkout regression:** Extending `HoldPicker` touches the existing purchase path. The GA DOM/body regression, existing countdown tests, `make check`, and browser page containing both performance kinds catch it.
5. **Large-map DOM and layout cost:** Two thousand semantic buttons increase hydration and layout work, especially on mobile. A browser fixture at representative scale and performance profiling catch unacceptable behavior; SVG is not adopted without an accessible interaction design.
6. **Localization drift:** `UI_STRINGS` currently uses a permissive `Record<string, string>`. An explicit required-key test across `LOCALES` catches omissions without broadening this ticket into a localization-type refactor.
7. **Browser-only routing failure:** Unit tests mock `fetch` and smoke does not hydrate or click the island. The required browser reserve and conflict submissions catch gateway-prefix, CSP, bundle, and runtime failures.

## 7. Open decisions

No blocking contract or backend decision remains.

- **Large-map interaction beyond scrolling:** There is no performance budget, zoom model, or virtualization primitive at HEAD. Take accessible, scrollable section grids for TKT-174 and record a follow-up only if the representative 2,000-seat browser check is materially slow.
- **Browser fixture identity:** The repository has no durable seated demo fixture. Create it through existing APIs during verification and use its returned `event.id`; do not add seed data or an e2e harness.
- **Polling scale versus freshness:** Take the contract-aligned five-second poll required by ADR-006. Do not silently lengthen it or introduce a frontend cache to compensate for TKT-31’s undeployed shared/hot-event tier.

<!-- sdlc:stage=plan-review kind=plan -->
### Adversarial plan critique — TKT-174

**Critiqued by `main-agent` (Claude Opus 5)**, per `config.models.planReview`. Cross-model check holds.

The strongest of the three drafts in this epic. Its central architectural claim is not merely plausible — it is the decided architecture, quoted below. Three amendments follow, all about scope and failure states rather than about the design.

#### Existence audit at `b7745cca`

| Named | Exists |
|---|---|
| `web/backoffice/test/SeatMapEditor.test.tsx` + `@testing-library/react`/`jsdom` in back office **and** scanner | ✅ — adding the harness to the storefront follows an in-repo pattern, as claimed |
| `UI_STRINGS: Record<Locale, Record<string, string>>` | ✅ — and the permissive `Record<string, string>` is exactly why the draft's required-key test is needed |
| `seat_map_id` and `SeatMapGeometry` in `web/storefront/src/lib/api-types.gen.ts` | ✅ both, regenerated by TKT-172 |
| `remainingMilliseconds` exported and unit-tested | ✅ `web/storefront/test/hold-picker.test.ts` |
| `Seat.seat_identity` served directly by the geometry read | ✅ — the picker never composes `section/row/seat` itself, which is right: composition is server-side and ADR-029 governs it |

**No hallucinated seams.**

#### The central claim — verified, and stronger than the draft argued

The draft fetches geometry and occupancy **browser-side**, keeps occupancy out of `PageDataCache`, and polls at 5s. I went to check whether "ADR-006 explicitly places availability in a seconds-tier island" was a real citation or a convenient one. It is real, and nearly verbatim:

> *"page HTML at the minutes tier with availability as a **seconds-tier React island** (headers captured through real nginx)"*
> *"availability as a React island **polling the seconds tier**"*
> *"fresh-API mismatch impossible by construction (**availability is structurally absent from cached HTML**)"*

That last line also answers the event page's single-source-rule comment, which I had expected to be the draft's weak point: the rule exists so a *cached copy* of the page's own data cannot go stale against a fresher API read. Occupancy is not in the page HTML at all. The draft reached that answer independently.

ADR-006 also names this exact ticket: *"TKT-35 seat picker stays React."*

#### Finding 1 — AMEND: one checkout path is not the same as one file

The draft puts geometry fetching, occupancy fetching, the 5s poll, selection state, the conflict merge, the seated reservation body, the countdown and the checkout form **all in `HoldPicker.tsx`** — today an 88-line component — with `SeatMapPicker.tsx` reduced to a presentational grid.

Its reason for rejecting a *sibling* island is correct and I accept it: a sibling that later mounts `HoldPicker` would duplicate reservation state and create the seated checkout fork AC3 forbids. But that argument is about **state ownership**, and it does not require a single file.

**Amendment A1:** `SeatMapPicker` owns the seat concern end to end — geometry, occupancy, the poll, selection, and the conflict merge — and reports the selected identities upward. `HoldPicker` keeps reservation and checkout and gains only: two optional props, "am I seated", the selected identities, and the seated request body. Still one island, still one hydration boundary, still one reservation state. The seated concern becomes independently testable and independently readable, and the GA path's file barely moves — which matters for AC5 and for finding 2.

#### Finding 2 — AMEND: do not migrate the GA checkout's strings in this ticket

The draft moves *all* of `HoldPicker`'s inline strings into `UI_STRINGS` — including the name, email, fake-payment, service-failure and pending-payment text — reasoning that seated mode would otherwise expose English fragments in French.

Check the premise: those fragments are **already** hardcoded English today, in the shipped GA checkout, in both locales (`<label>Name …`, `<label>Email …`, `<label>Fake payment …`). This ticket does not create that defect and does not worsen it. What the draft proposes is a refactor of the working checkout path, bundled into the diff that also introduces seat selection — which is precisely the combination that makes a regression hard to attribute.

**Amendment A2:** in scope — the **new** seat-picker strings, in both locales, plus the required-key test the draft designed. Out of scope — migrating the existing checkout-form strings. Filed as an incidental instead. AC6 says *"Both locales carry the new strings"*, and this satisfies it exactly.

#### Finding 3 — GAP: no failure state for the two new reads, and the obvious fallback is dangerous

The draft handles *skew* (mismatched `slot_id`/`seat_map_id` → fail closed) but never says what the card does when geometry or occupancy simply **fails**: a 5xx, a network error, or the 404 that TKT-172's own risk register predicted —

> *"Catalog can expose seating before the publication consumer has provisioned inventory, temporarily yielding inventory 404 … a 404 from this endpoint is not necessarily 'no such slot'."*

That is not hypothetical: the draft's own browser-verification step 2 says *"wait until seat occupancy returns 200"*, which concedes the window exists.

The dangerous part is that the most natural recovery is wrong. **Falling back to the quantity picker on a seated performance is guaranteed to fail**: a quantity hold against a seated pool is refused by `ErrPoolKindMismatch` → 409, every time. A buyer would get a working-looking control that can never succeed.

**Amendment A3:** define the failure state explicitly. A seated card that cannot load geometry or occupancy renders a legible, localized "seat selection is temporarily unavailable" state with no purchase control — **never** the quantity picker, and never an empty map that reads as a sold-out house. A transient occupancy failure *after* a successful first load keeps the last known map and says so, rather than blanking it. One test per case.

#### Accepted without change

- **Real `<button>` elements over SVG.** The draft's reason is the right one: making thousands of SVG shapes keyboard-operable and self-describing recreates native button semantics badly. AC1's "not colour alone" and AC2's assistive-technology requirement come free.
- **5s poll, never faster; paused when hidden; stopped after a successful hold.** Matches the contract's own `max-age=5`. The draft is also honest that this does not close TKT-31's undeployed shared-cache gap, and refuses to invent a frontend cache to compensate — correct.
- **Conflict handling**: union the lost identities immediately, keep non-contended selections, name them in the existing polite live region, and sequence/abort so an older poll cannot revert the conflict. That last detail is the one most likely to be skipped and most likely to produce an unreproducible bug.
- **`remaining_capacity` as a ceiling**: not displayed as "N seats available", not re-subtracted, zero disables selection, and a ceiling that drops below an existing selection preserves the selection but disables Reserve. This is the correct reading of the field TKT-173's review made me rename.
- **ID-equality validation against props, failing closed** — the same instinct that closed TKT-173's high finding.
- **Test seam**: jsdom + `@testing-library/react` in the storefront, plus pure helpers (`orderByPosition`, `selectionCeiling`, `applySeatConflict`) tested directly, following the `remainingMilliseconds` precedent.

#### Pre-mortem

1. **The GA path breaks and nobody notices until checkout.** Mitigated by A1 (the GA file barely changes) and A2 (its strings do not move at all); the GA regression test and a browser page carrying both performance kinds are the catch.
2. **The picker renders an empty map during the provisioning window** and reads as sold out. → A3.
3. **A stale poll un-does a conflict.** The draft names it; the out-of-order mocked-response test is what proves the sequencing.
4. **The browser check is done on a 3-seat map** and the 2000-button risk is asserted rather than measured. → the browser fixture should include one section large enough to be honest about it.
5. **`aria-pressed` on a disabled button.** A taken seat must be `disabled` and *not* pressed; a selected seat `aria-pressed="true"`. Easy to conflate, invisible without a screen reader.

#### Verdict

**ACCEPT with amendments A1, A2, A3.** No part rejected. The architecture stands and is better-founded than the draft claimed.

#### TDD

`web/storefront/test/SeatMapPicker.test.tsx` was written first and observed red (the module did not exist), then the component made it green. 30 storefront tests now pass: 10 component tests in jsdom plus the pure helpers (`orderByPosition`, `selectionCeiling`, `applySeatConflict`) and the pre-existing countdown/format/cache suites.

Two harness notes, recorded because they shaped the tests:
- **The storefront had no DOM harness.** Added `jsdom` + `@testing-library/react`, following the back office and scanner, which both already carry them. A `vitest.config.ts` mirroring the back office keeps `node` the default so the existing pure-function tests are untouched.
- **jest-dom matchers are not in this repo.** `toBeDisabled`/`toHaveAttribute` failed; rather than add another dependency, the assertions use plain DOM (`(el as HTMLButtonElement).disabled`, `el.getAttribute(...)`).

#### The browser verification earned its place

AC7 is this repo's binding rule and it was not a formality. **It found a defect no test could.**

`.hold-picker button` — a pre-existing global rule — paints a solid accent block at specificity **(0,1,1)**, which beats a bare `.seat` at **(0,1,0)**. So every **free** seat rendered in the accent colour, *identical to a selected one*. `.seat.selected` at (0,2,0) still won, which is precisely what made the result look deliberate rather than broken.

Nothing in the suite could see it: the component was correct, the DOM was correct, the accessible names were correct, and a screen reader would have read the map perfectly. It was the **cascade** that was wrong. Fixed in `9338e65d` by scoping the seat rules under `.seat-map`; verified by reading computed styles back over CDP rather than by eye — free `rgb(255,255,255)`, selected `rgb(15,76,129)`, taken `var(--line)`.

A second trap: the first re-check still showed the old colours because the page is **minutes-tier cached** and the browser served it from cache. The fix was real; the observation was stale. `Network.setCacheDisabled` settled it.

#### Browser evidence

Driven with headless Chrome over the DevTools Protocol against `make up` — no harness added to the repo, the driver lives in the session scratchpad. Node 24's global `WebSocket` means CDP needed no dependency.

- **Happy path**: island hydrated, both reads 200, two seats clicked, toggle verified, Reserve clicked → `POST /api/commerce/reservations` **201** with `seat_identities` and **no** `quantity`, countdown and checkout appeared, payment completed to a ticket link. The GA performance on the same page still showed its quantity input.
- **Conflict path**: two seats selected, a rival claimed one out-of-band, Reserve clicked → **409**, message `"No longer available: Stalls/A/3"`, the lost seat re-rendered as taken, and **the non-contended seat stayed selected**.
- **Polling**: an incidental run proved it unaided — a rival's claim appeared on the map without a reload.
- **FR**: legend, seat labels, status line and button all localized (`"0 place(s) sur 3 sélectionnée(s)"`, `"Réserver les places"`).

#### Deviations from the plan

1. **Styles were initially skipped.** The plan named `[eventId].astro` for the map styles and the first commit did not include them — the picker rendered as an unstyled bullet list. Caught by the browser check, not by review. Added in `9338e65d`.
2. **The conflict channel is a `window` CustomEvent** keyed by slot id (`seat-conflict:${slotId}`), so `HoldPicker` can hand a 409's identities to `SeatMapPicker` without either owning the other's state. The plan did not specify a mechanism. This is the least-coupled option available given A1's split, and the key is slot-scoped so two performances on one page cannot cross-talk — but it is a global event bus in miniature and it is flagged for review.
